pharm: Cyclic heptapeptide platelet aggregation inhibitor that reversibly blocks the platelet GP IIb/IIIa receptor, preventing fibrinogen binding and platelet aggregation.
quick: 180 mcg/kg IV bolus, then 2 mcg/kg/min infusion
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
CrCl <50 mL/min: reduce infusion to 1 mcg/kg/min; dialysis-dependent contraindicated
summary: Eptifibatide is an intravenous glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor used in acute coronary syndrome and during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to reduce death and ischemic events. It is given as a weight-based bolus followed by a continuous infusion, with infusion-rate reduction for CrCl <50 mL/min. The principal risk is bleeding; it is contraindicated in active bleeding, recent major surgery/stroke, severe uncontrolled hypertension, and dialysis dependence.
indications: Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/NSTEMI) managed medically or with PCI - to decrease combined endpoint of death or new MI
Patients undergoing PCI including intracoronary stenting - to decrease death, new MI, or need for urgent intervention

dosage.t: Bolus ASAP after diagnosis; infuse until discharge/CABG, up to 72 h
dosage.n: If PCI performed, continue up to 18-24 h after, max 96 h total

dosage.d: 180 mcg/kg bolus, then 2 mcg/kg/min, plus a second 180 mcg/kg bolus 10 min after the first
dosage.t: Continue infusion until discharge or up to 18-24 h

admin: Give bolus by IV push, followed by continuous IV infusion
Obtain baseline hematocrit/hemoglobin, platelet count, serum creatinine, PT/aPTT before infusion; ACT if PCI
Maintain aPTT 50-70 seconds (unless PCI); for PCI maintain ACT 200-300 seconds with heparin
Reduce infusion to 1 mcg/kg/min if CrCl <50 mL/min
May be co-administered with heparin and aspirin; monitor closely to minimize bleeding
moa: Reversibly binds the platelet glycoprotein (GP) IIb/IIIa receptor, blocking binding of fibrinogen, von Willebrand factor, and other adhesive ligands, thereby inhibiting the final common pathway of platelet aggregation. Effect reverses within hours of stopping infusion as platelet function recovers.

absolute: History of bleeding diathesis or active abnormal bleeding within previous 30 days
Severe uncontrolled hypertension (SBP >200 or DBP >110 mmHg) not controlled on therapy
Stroke within 30 days or any history of hemorrhagic stroke
Current/planned use of another parenteral GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor
Hypersensitivity to eptifibatide or any component

preg: Limited human data; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Not known whether excreted in human milk; exercise caution.
renal: Reduce infusion rate to 1 mcg/kg/min when CrCl <50 mL/min (bolus unchanged). Contraindicated in dialysis-dependent patients. Eptifibatide is substantially renally cleared.
hepatic: No specific dosing data; not metabolized substantially by the liver.

major: Other antiplatelets/anticoagulants (heparin, warfarin, thrombolytics, other GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors) - additive bleeding risk
Concurrent parenteral GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor - contraindicated
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor aPTT/ACT when used with heparin; obtain baseline platelet count and recheck for thrombocytopenia.

monitoring: Platelet count (baseline and within ~6 h of starting; watch for acute thrombocytopenia)
aPTT (50-70 s) or ACT (200-300 s during PCI)
Signs and symptoms of bleeding at all sites including access site
counsel: This medicine prevents blood clots and is given by vein in hospital
Report any unusual bleeding, bruising, blood in urine/stool, or severe headache immediately
The team will monitor your blood counts and kidney function
Tell staff about all blood thinners and recent surgery or stroke
Bleeding risk is higher at vascular access sites - keep the area still as instructed
pk: Immediate platelet inhibition after IV bolus
Platelet function recovers ~4-8 h after stopping infusion
Refrigerate 2-8 C; protect from light; may store at room temperature for limited time per label
pearls: Bleeding is the principal hazard - watch vascular access sites and check platelets early
Reversible, short-acting GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor; effect wears off within hours of stopping
Bolus is unchanged but infusion is halved (1 mcg/kg/min) when CrCl <50 mL/min
Acute profound thrombocytopenia can occur - check platelet count within ~6 hours of starting
missed: Continuous IV infusion in acute care; not patient-administered. If infusion is interrupted, restart per protocol with clinical reassessment - do not give an extra bolus unless directed.
overdose: Excessive dosing increases bleeding risk. There is no specific antidote; eptifibatide can be removed by hemodialysis. Stop the infusion, provide supportive care, transfuse platelets/blood products as needed for serious bleeding.
